summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Atsuki Nakagami has served as a visiting researcher at the University of Hamburg (attested 2022) and was affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Atsushi Ibuki studied at Waseda University from circa 1978 to 1989. A scholar of Buddhist studies, he became a professor at Toyo University around 2007.

Atsushi Kanazawa studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1980) and works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He taught at the Meteorological College (~1989–1993) before serving as associate professor (~1995–2004) and continuing at Komazawa University (~2004).

Atsushi Kiyozawa, an expert in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completed his doctoral studies at the University of Delhi (~1978–1984). He was appointed as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).

Atsushi Uno studied Indology and philosophy at Kyoto University and Banaras Hindu University, supervised by T. R. V. Murti. He taught at Shuchiin, Kyoto, and Tokai universities before holding professorships at Hiroshima University (1974–1986) and Kindai University (~1986–1993).

Atsuuji Ashikaga studied at Doshisha and Kyoto universities, learning under Ryosaburo Sakaki. He specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, serving as professor at Kyoto University (1950) and president of the Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan (~1975–1983).
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He taught at Otani University, where he is attested as a lecturer in 1990 and as a professor in 2014.

Atul Chandra Chatterjee studied under Charles Henry Tawney at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University (~1888–1892), later attending King's College, Cambridge (~1893–1896). A specialist in Indology and history, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1897–1931).

August Boeckh, an expert in history, archaeology, and linguistics, studied at Halle-Wittenberg under F. A. Wolf and F. Schleiermacher. He held posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and the Humboldt University of Berlin (1811–1861).

August Conrady, a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology, studied at Würzburg and Leipzig. He taught at Peking University (1903–1904) and held posts at the University of Leipzig from 1891, becoming a full professor in 1920.

August Dillmann studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Tübingen (~1840–1845). A scholar of linguistics and religious studies, he held positions at Tübingen (~1851–1864), Kiel (~1864–1869), Giessen (~1869), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1869–1894).

August Ferdinand Naeke, a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology, studied at the University of Leipzig (~1806–1810). He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Bonn (~1818–1838).

August Fick studied linguistics and Indology under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (1852–1856). He served as associate professor of comparative linguistics at Göttingen (1876) and full professor at the University of Breslau (1888–1891).

August Fischer studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1885–1889). Working in linguistics, he held a post at the University of Leipzig (~1900–1930) and served on the board of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1900–1930).

August Friedrich Pott studied at Göttingen and under Franz Bopp in Berlin. A specialist in linguistics and Indology, he taught at Berlin before serving as professor of general linguistics at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1833.

August Hermann Francke studied at Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and the Humboldt University of Berlin. Specializing in Tibetology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, he served as Privatdozent (1922) and extraordinary professor (1925) at the Humboldt University of Berlin.

August Hjalmar Edgren studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and under William Dwight Whitney at Yale. Working in linguistics and Indology, he held posts at Yale, Lund, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and served as Rector at the University of Gothenburg (1891–1893).

August Johan Bernet Kempers studied at Leiden University (~1924–1933). Focusing on history, archaeology, and Indology, he directed the Pusat Penelitian Arkeologi Nasional (~1947–1956) and worked at the Netherlands Open Air Museum (1958–1971) and University of Amsterdam (1969–1984).

August Leskien studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. A scholar of linguistics and Indology, he taught at Göttingen and Jena before becoming a professor at the University of Leipzig (1870–1915).

August Schleicher studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Bonn, learning under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and others. A specialist in linguistics and Indology, he held posts at Bonn (1846), Charles University (1850–1857), and the University of Jena (1857).
